messages.author: 7b72881378080971
messages.subject: Joint models problem
parts:
Hi all,

I am trying to model some disease data at two levels to make some cross-scale predictions. I have the numbers of infected individuals within a catchment area and I have the covariate values of the pixels within those catchment areas. I would like to try and estimate coefficients for the pixel level covariates. So I have 2 equations which link these two levels:

1) a poisson regression with the number of infected individuals per pixel (unknown) being dependent on the pixel level covariates (known) 
2) The number of infected individuals per catchment area (known) being the sum of the unknown number of infected individuals per pixel within the catchment.

I can't work out how to specify this in INLA to estimate the pixel level coefficients. I realise that I may have to account for spatial autocorrelation between catchments (and pixels) down the line but wanted to get a basic model up and running first. Any guidance would be fantastic. I've included some toy code which might help explain my problem better. 

Thanks very much,
Hugh

# toy data
set.seed(1)
# Pixel level data
Pixel_Catch_ID<-c(rep(1,5),rep(2,5),rep(3,10),rep(4,5))
Pixel_Population<-rpois(25,1000)
Pixel_Covar1<-runif(25,0,1)
Pixel_Covar2<-runif(25,0,1)
Ninf_Pix<-NA ### This is not known
Pixel_Data<-data.frame(Pixel_Catch_ID,Pixel_Population,Pixel_Covar1,Pixel_Covar2,Ninf_Pix)

# Catchment level data
Catch_ID<-1:5
Ninf_Catch<-c(1,4,5,10,0) 
Catch_Data<-data.frame(Catch_ID,Ninf_Catch)

# The number of infections per catchment is equal to the sum of the 
# number of infections per pixel i.e.
Ninf_Catch = tapply(Ninf_Pix,Pixel_Catch_ID,sum)

# The number of infections per pixel is dependent on relationship with pixel level covariates (which are known)
log(Ninf_Pix) = alpha + beta1*Pixel_Covar1 + beta2*Pixel_Covar2 + offset(Pixel_Population)

# I want estimates of alpha, beta1 and beta2

messages.author: b453c29749de564d
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Joint models problem
parts:
Thanks for your email.

It looks to me that Ninf_Pix is an integer >= 0 hence cannot be fit, as
we only can do continous variables. However, there may be ways around
it, approximately.

I would like to see the math of the model to answer for sure, please
send that as a pdf and we can discuss it further.

Best
H

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Joint models problem
parts:
Dear Håvard,

Many thanks for your email. 

Yes Ninf_Pix would be an integer >=0. I have written out the math of the approach in the attached pdf (option 1). 

I think there is an alternative approach using logistic regression and have included this in the pdf (option 2). I would be interested to know whether you think this is a viable approach.

I am not a mathematician so forgive me if my wording/formulae look a little naive..Hopefully I've explained the problem in enough detail but if not I'm happy to elaborate.

Thanks again for your input, I'm hopeful I can find an INLA solution as I think this is possible with MCMC in Winbugs (but no doubt it will be slow..).

Regards,
Hugh
